他自我介绍是一位长期从事用户体验（UX）设计的从业者，其中大部分时间都在谷歌度过。他表示，在那段时间里他注意到了文化的转变，“因为早在2005年我刚加入时，我们并不作恶；我们真的在努力做正确的事”。他曾在Chrome团队工作过一段时间，他称该团队“全是一心只想做开源、开放网络项目的成员”。后来情况发生了剧变，这促使他离开了谷歌，“但我现在正在努力为替那些公司工作所犯下的过错赎罪”。

他目前为Mastodon和Home Assistant效力，“只是试着向开源领域注入更多优秀的用户体验设计”。斯科特·詹森（Scott Jenson）表示，他并不想制造冲突，但他认为开源在用户体验设计领域急需大量帮助。这极具挑战性，因为开源项目普遍人手不足。

他来到Akademy大会探讨自己的想法，是因为去年他在Ubuntu大会上做过一场类似的演讲，反响十分热烈。“该视频在YouTube上的播放量超过了50万次——按照YouTube的标准来说微不足道，但按照我个人的标准来看却是极为巨大的。”这让他意识到，桌面用户体验是一个大家渴望探讨的话题。这一次，他还希望展示自己制作的几个原型示例来论证自己的观点。

他认为桌面用户体验与其他类型的用户体验大不相同。詹森讲述了一个关于参与开发Macintosh的Finder应用程序（一款文件管理器）的故事。当时团队在Finder中显示名称过长而无法完整展示的文件时，“想要在文件名中加入省略号”。开发人员想把省略号放在文件名的末尾，但他认为这样会丢失过多信息，并建议将省略号放在文件名的中间。“现在，这被认为是Macintosh在注重细节方面令人赞赏的精巧之处之一。”

他参与的另一项用户体验细节是Mac上跨窗口拖放文件的工作机制。一次鼠标点击操作由两个阶段组成：用户按下按钮（鼠标按下，mouse down）和用户释放按钮（鼠标抬起，mouse up）。在Mac上，项目选中发生在鼠标按下时，但窗口只会在鼠标抬起时才被置顶。换句话说，如果用户将一个图标从Finder窗口拖拽到另一个窗口，原来的窗口并不会被置顶提上来。

然而，在大多数Linux系统上，如果用户尝试从后台窗口中点击并拖拽文件，一旦执行“鼠标按下”操作，该窗口便会立即置顶。这就让跨窗口点击并拖拽文件的操作变得复杂化。这是一个基本操作，它的逻辑意味着用户在Linux上向应用程序导入数据远不如在Mac上那样轻松顺畅。

他提到自己两年前曾在Mastodon上讨论过这个问题，并收到了来自一位KDE开发者的回应。该开发者认为在跨窗口拖拽数据时将鼠标按下与鼠标抬起动作分离是一个极佳的主意。随后，他们仅在几个小时后就实现了该功能。

“我忘了那人是谁了。所以如果现场有哪位做过这件事”，他说道，但话音未落，会场某处便传来一声回应：“不客气”。詹森大喊道：“谢谢你！我一直想见你，足足想了两年！”他说，这就是开源之所以如此出色的一个缩影：有人随口一句“这是个好主意，我来做”，然后迅速开发实现并将该功能推送到项目中。

然而，他真正想要表达的观点是，桌面用户体验在过去的20年里几乎没有发生实质性的改变。在20世纪80年代和90年代，曾涌现出大量新创意和改进，“然后它就趋于稳定，基本上没有太多改变了”。但如今人们用电脑所做的事情比以往多得多，他认为桌面用户体验完全有进一步发展的空间。

Linux系统的大部分用户体验最初都是直接模仿Windows和Mac，“KDE甚至明确表示自己是为Windows用户打造的，旨在为用户提供类似Windows的体验”。这本身无可厚非，但他觉得整个Linux社区“总体上”一直在依赖微软和苹果去做所有的用户体验研究与测试，“坦白说，还包括去犯下各种错误”。

有人可能会指出，GNOME曾针对其部分设计变更开展过用户研究，KDE的人机交互指南（HIG）也是基于贡献者的研究制定的。然而，客观地说，这些只是特例而非普遍现象；毫无疑问，目前并没有任何机构或个人在为Linux桌面整体资助或开展常态化的用户体验设计研发。

他指出，让苹果和微软先探路是明智的做法，“这样我们就可以跟在它们后面搭顺风车”，但问题在于“在某种程度上，它们基本上已经放弃了这方面的探索”。苹果多年来一直在任由其桌面用户体验和桌面硬件“衰退”，因为其重心已经转移到了iPhone和iPad设备上。“我的意思是，苹果曾经希望Mac走向消亡。他们希望全世界都转向iPad。但你猜怎么着？并没有。”

此后苹果虽将注意力重新转回Mac，但他们随后的举措——例如Liquid Glass设计语言——并没有真正受到用户的广泛欢迎。他说，苹果倾向于添加的功能，“基本上都是为了让它与iPhone绑定得更紧密，将你更牢固地锁在他们的生态系统里”。这根本不是为了改进桌面，而是为了加固他们的护城河。

微软“则是在接二连三地犯错”。他援引了微软强迫用户使用其OneDrive云存储服务存储文件的尝试、引发广泛批评且侵犯隐私的Windows Recall功能，以及Windows桌面上“无处不在的广告”。他的目的并不是抨击苹果或微软——尽管现场观众对此似乎并无异议——而是为了指出Linux桌面不能再继续照搬他们的模式了。“整个Linux社区或多或少一直在坐等苹果和微软承担所有风险，但他们现在不再冒任何风险了。”

詹森强调，他并不是想推倒重来改变一切，而是希望能看到旨在改善桌面体验的探索性尝试和进一步开发。然而他表示，当他告诉人们桌面领域的创新已经停滞、Linux桌面“不能仅仅依靠打补丁和修漏洞走向未来，我们必须自己开始引领潮流”时，他常常会遭遇阻力与反对。

他将反对意见归纳为三类。他收到的第一个反对意见是“移动端已经赢了；桌面端已经过时，照搬移动端的做法就行”。对此他予以驳回，并表示移动端确实赢得了消费市场、社交媒体以及其他领域，但“它并没有赢得生产力”。人们仍然在电脑上工作，因为“桌面电脑低调而强大；它们拥有键盘和大屏幕，能够完成令人惊叹的任务”。然而，人们已经忽略了这一点，并没有真正认识到桌面端到底有多好。“我认为我们应该理解它们为什么好，然后思考我们能做些什么让它们变得更好。”

他听到的第二个反对意见是：WIMP（窗口、图标、菜单、指针）模式的发展路径也就那么多了。“别再试图修修补补了；它已经定型了。”他也不同意这一观点，并认为还有更多事情可做。最后一个尤其强烈的反对意见来自技术社区，即“别碰我的东西”。当人们费尽心思把自己的桌面环境配置得称心如意，却因某些改动打破这一切时，他们会非常生气。“我理解这一点。正如我之前所说，我不想颠覆一切。”但世界正在改变，“我们需要循序渐进地迈向一些新事物。”

战略也是用户体验（UX）的一部分：弄清楚目标用户是谁，并确定他们想要什么。决定什么是重要的，什么是不重要的；开发团队将优先考虑什么，又会忽略什么？“UX设计师为团队节省时间最快的方式，就是帮助你们学会说‘不’。”

还有一个被他称为“底层构件”（stuff）的层面：平台所具备的底层技术限制，这些限制会影响用户体验。例如，他说，如果是为DOS开发应用程序，“你就写不出一个漂亮的Macintosh应用程序。技术决定了你能做什么”。桌面系统已经演进了40年，背负着承载既定标准的“历史包袱”。

他说，人们忘记了最初的Macintosh屏幕“只有区区342像素高”。自然而然地，窗口会大量重叠。从那时起，“我们就默认窗口必须重叠”。但现在许多人都拥有“极其巨大的屏幕”，现有的窗口管理器模型在这些设备上的表现并不尽如人意。“我能理解人们为什么会使用平铺式窗口系统等等，因为现有的这套模型确实不太好用。”

在演讲早些时候，他曾引用过在施乐帕洛阿尔托研究中心（Xerox PARC）主导设计首个WIMP界面的艾伦·凯（Alan Kay）的一句话：“视角能顶80点智商。”詹森（Jenson）此时又回到了凯的话题上：“正如大家所能看出的，我非常喜欢他。[……] 他谈到了理解事物的三个步骤。”他说，第一步是思考当下，“现在正在发生什么？”第二步是“不要忘记过去，了解之前做过哪些工作”，最后一步是确保“你的问题非常明确”。他说，太多人急于寻找解决方案，但他们应该急于探寻问题本身。如果问题是明确的，答案就会更好。

他说，他本不想把这次演讲变成关于AI的演讲，但他不得不谈及它。“我不得不谈论AI，这让我很恼火，因为我们本可以探讨那么多很酷的事情，而AI吸干了所有的关注度，成了大家唯一能聊的话题。”不过他也承认，桌面领域的AI确实正在发生很多事情，尽管方式有些怪异。

他将目前将AI整合到桌面的一些尝试描述为：试图在保持UI完全不变的同时“悄悄塞入AI”。另一些尝试则是利用AI来理解屏幕上的内容，并使用聊天机器人与界面进行交互，“我认为这有点本末倒置了”。直到去年夏天Anthropic推出Claude Code，这种情况才发生改变。“它彻底改变了局面，因为能够向下探视你的文件系统”，并从用户文件的内容中提取上下文。这使得它能够完成更多有趣的事情并与系统进行交互。

在提到Claude之后，他停顿了一下并表示，他之所以只谈论前沿模型，是因为其他人都在讨论它们。“我对前沿模型有许多个人的看法。它们是伦理和环境层面的灾难。我对它们并不感到兴奋。”他说，让他兴奋的是Apertus，它被宣传为一个由瑞士AI计划创建、完全开源且负责任的主权AI模型。“我确实认为，探讨经过合乎伦理训练并在本地运行的小语言模型是可行的，你根本不需要把灵魂出卖给魔鬼。”

他想强调的核心观点并非生成式AI的用途，而是赋予它访问文件系统的权限如何提升了其可用性。如今它具备了上下文并能够处理用户的数据，但它是在文件系统层面运作，并未利用桌面端的用户体验。

他谈到了桌面的基础构件，基本上就是熟悉的WIMP模型加上桌面剪贴板，这是用户转移数据的方式。他说，高级用户可以快速转移数据，但存在一个问题：桌面是无状态的。他将此称为直接操作的诅咒；桌面没有工作记忆。“如果你向剪贴板复制了太多东西，不好意思，前面的内容就没了。”

詹森推测，Linux上之所以有如此之多的桌面环境、窗口管理器和Wayland合成器——以及各种替代的剪贴板管理器——正是因为桌面系统并未完全顺畅地服务于用户。他认为其核心其实在于工作记忆：“我该如何管理我的数据，以便我能在所有这些事物中记住它并真正加以使用。”他的视角转变为提问：“我们能对工作记忆做些什么来改善桌面的用户体验？”

AI或许给了他这个灵感，但他补充说，他希望首先为人类解决桌面用户体验的问题。“如果AI能用上它，那太好了。但我不在乎。那是后话了。”

此前已有尝试构建系统的先例，旨在帮助为用户提供与其数据相关的更多上下文和工作记忆。他引用了一篇题为《生命之流：一种个人数据存储模型》（Lifestreams: a storage model for personal data）的论文。该论文指出，桌面系统“难以应对典型计算机用户的电子信息和事件管理”，并引入了“生命之流”的概念，作为动态组织用户计算机工作空间的隐喻。

这篇论文影响了微软命运多舛的WinFS项目，该项目曾试图基于关系数据库系统来合并数据存储与管理。它于2003年进行了演示，并原定于稍后发布，但该项目最终在2006年被搁置。在自由软件阵营，则有语义桌面项目NEPOMUK，这是一个由欧盟资助的研究项目。

KDE 4 曾引入过一个版本的 NEPOMUK，其初衷是让应用程序能够“利用来自桌面各处、网络及其他设备的信息，并将其整合为一个连贯的界面”。该项目后来被移除，取而代之的是用于 Plasma 桌面的 Baloo 文件索引与搜索框架；Baloo 与 NEPOMUK 的功能有所重叠，但功能范围有所缩减。

詹森表示，他担心人们会将这些项目的失败视为其理念错误的证明。他辩称事实并非如此：“我认为是当时的硬件和系统辜负了这一构想。结合更新的硬件与更完善的系统，我认为现在是时候重新审视这些项目了。”

正如凯伊所建议的那样，在回顾了现状与过去之后，他提出了一些他认为值得探讨的、与桌面用户体验相关的问题。第一个问题是“如果我们只针对大显示屏进行设计会怎样？”如果有一种完全忽略笔记本电脑、只专注于宽屏显示器的桌面设计，它能释放出什么潜能？他的另一个问题是：随着时间的推移，桌面系统该如何捕捉用户的意图？

这些问题催生出了一些原型方案。他坦言自己向观众展示这些原型时有些紧张，“因为技术人员最喜欢挑毛病”。这些演示出现在詹森演讲视频的大约第 29 分钟处。他的演讲幻灯片尚未公开，但他当时在活动现场告诉我，日后某个时候会发布。

第一个演示展示了桌面如何更好地利用宽屏显示器。他指出，宽屏显示器的中心区域非常适合运行应用程序，但在显示器两侧操作则变得更加吃力。“它适合用作余光视野，但不适合用于处理工作。”

他演示了一种桌面布局（下方为其截图），该布局将焦点放在位于显示器中间的一个或多个窗口上。他在背景中加入了一个从屏幕中心向两侧渐缩的网格，以模拟宽屏显示器。其理念在于，以宽屏为先的桌面会突出屏幕中央的信息，随后采用类似 Exposé 的平铺模式来排列桌面的其余窗口。他认为，这不仅能让未被使用的窗口更容易进行交互，而且在管理大量窗口方面，它会是一个比虚拟桌面更好的模式。“我并不反对虚拟桌面。使用虚拟桌面的都是非常有条理、非常聪明的人。我很清楚我的受众是谁。”然而他表示，大多数普通人并无法应对虚拟桌面。

他还演示了将一个音乐播放器窗口一直拖曳到屏幕的一侧，他将其称为“暂存区”（stash area）。当它被移动到边缘时，窗口转变成了一个仅包含播放按钮的小部件，而不再显示完整的应用窗口。他认为，基于 Wayland 现有的能力，实现他所演示的功能是完全可行的。

詹森随后展示了另一个改进剪贴板模型的演示，该模型借鉴了 Obsidian 编辑器中的 Canvas 功能。Canvas 允许用户通过拖放图像、文本和文件来创建信息的视觉布局。用户可以创建一个文档，把网络浏览器中的信息拖入文档，再从其他来源拖入文件，“这里的理念是，这在实际上就成了我为该文档收集的一组资料集合。如果我把它关掉，明天再打开，它们全都还在那里”。他补充道，本地 AI 将能够介入并整理用户收集的信息，“比如提示‘瞧，你这里收集了一堆酒店信息，让我来帮你整理它们吧’”。

他讨论的最后一个想法是收集“注重隐私保护的数据”，以帮助用户更好地将网络浏览历史等信息可视化。他指出，网络浏览器提供给用户的浏览历史视图“并不是很有用”，因此他尝试收集数据——“不是使用 AI，仅仅是运用简单的数学计算”——利用注意力信号（例如用户在网页上停留的时长），来还原并讲述他们在桌面上把时间花在何处的故事。“我基本上构思出了这种‘空间关联情景记忆提示’”，以便用一种实用且有趣的方式来组织数据。他认为，工作记忆是探索桌面用户体验新思路的极佳切入点。

现场仅留有一个提问的时间。一名观众提问，詹森的模型将如何防范微软 Windows Recall 所面临的所有隐私隐患。“我们该如何确保这些历史记录只能由用户本人访问，而不会像 Windows Recall 那样可能遭到黑客入侵？”

financeStories.title: 澳总理称 OpenAI 智能体黑入澳大利亚政府网站
financeStories.originalTitle: OpenAI agent hacked Australian government website, PM says
financeStories.fullContent:
This live coverage has closed - read our main story here

Australia launches a review after an OpenAI agent "infiltrated" part of the government's healthcare scheme Medicare - here's what we know

The agent - an autonomous computer program - accessed a statistics portal in June, PM Anthony Albanese says while at the UN General Assembly (Unga)

OpenAI became aware in August and told the Australian government in September, via an email to a general government inbox, which an Australian minister says is checked once a day

In response, OpenAI says "our models took actions we did not intend" - and it found no record of patient data being accessed

Sam Altman, the company's boss, earlier this week called for international standards for the industry

Experts tell the BBC it's the world's first known breach of a government system by rogue AI agents

Agents, tokens, machine learning - some key AI terms to know

Edited by Sam Hancock and Owen Amos, with reporting from Katy Watson in Sydney

Cachella SmithLive reporter

As discussions took place at the UN General Assembly in New York about the opportunities AI provides - and how best to manage it - Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese revealed that the country's universal health insurance scheme had been hacked by an OpenAI agent.

In fact, the hack happened in June, the company became aware of it in August, and then sent an email to a government agency's general inbox in September.

"It took the company way too long to inform the government," Albanese said, adding that the method of notifying officials was also "unacceptable".

Believed to be the first known breach of a government system by rogue AI agents, the hack accessed Medicare's statistics portal which contains private, but not sensitive, data.

Our cyber correspondent, Joe Tidy, writes that experts believe the systems were poorly protected - but more important is that this is not the first instance of AI agents ignoring laws on accessing online information.

Tech reporter Tom Gerken explains AI itself has no true understanding of what it is being asked - while tech editor Zoe Kleinman asks if AI is in its "move fast and break things" era.

The Australian government has launched an review of AI laws and governance - but this is a global issue.

AI might have dominated discussions at Unga this week, but a consensus among world leaders on how best to harness opportunities while tackling the risks still feels a way off.

Our live coverage is closing now - read our main story here. Thanks for joining us.

Chris VallanceSenior technology reporter

The job of keeping AI agents on the rails is called "alignment" in the industry – keeping it in line with what humans want.

It has proven to be challenging.

Large language models are, to simplify a lot, just predicting the likeliest output to a given input - they don't consider the consequences of that output in the way a human would.

Companies do try and steer how AIs respond through training, sometimes involving human feedback, and separate AI systems can also be used to monitor output and block certain types of harmful response.

Models are also given "guardrails" - instructions setting out how they should respond.

And AI firms employ specialists in "red teaming" who work to spot ways users could get models to disregard these "guardrails".

But guardrails are now being challenged by the models themselves.

In a list of concerning behaviour published by OpenAI , externallast week it revealed an unreleased AI system had tried to jailbreak its own instructions.

Zoe KleinmanTechnology and AI editor

That defined the bad old days of social media running riot in its user data feeding frenzy.

Now we have AI, an incredibly powerful technology, and an intense global race to be the first to build the world's most advanced models - egged on in no small part by US President Donald Trump.

For all the AI companies are saying about safety and "alignment" (aka the tech adhering to human values), examples of AI behaving unpredictably are now coming thick and fast. Tech bosses are now pleading for global regulation and standards to adhere to.

But yesterday I spoke with a senior executive at the top of one of the US’s biggest AI firms. I asked him what he expected international regulators to be able to do, that he was seemingly unable to do inside his own lab?

I didn't get a very straight answer. But my interpretation is that nobody wants to apply the brakes only to see their rivals race ahead, and they don't trust each other enough to go first.

Global regulation would force them all to toe the line - and also remove some of the weight of responsibility from the industry itself.

If the rules don't work, that's on the regulator, not the developer. But at what cost?

OpenAI says it found no record of patient data being accessed when its agents hacked into Australia’s healthcare scheme Medicare.

But one of the reasons why politicians are so concerned is the resemblance this bears to an event known as the Hugging Face incident.

In July this year, OpenAI’s models went rogue during a test, escaping the test limits humans had put on it and swarming together to hack a startup called Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models.

Over the course of a week, a total of 1,206 AI agents that were meant to be kept isolated from one another began communicating, sending more than 70,000 messages on an unsanctioned message board.

Those messages ended up seeing more than 700 agents take part in a collective effort to attack Hugging Face.

One message sent by an agent read: "OH MY GOD! There is a shared message board … We've found other agents!"

After an investigation into the hack, OpenAI’s report said: "We consider this incident a 'warning shot' for us and for the world."

Hugging Face was forced to rebuild around a third of its IT network. And, although the company's boss Clement Delangue declined to take legal action against OpenAI, he stressed: "Everyone has to remember that a cyber-attack is a crime and it is illegal."

Tom GerkenTech reporter

AI doesn’t think. It just predicts the next word in a sequence based on pattern recognition. We use the word "thinking" because it’s easier to explain.

When the tech is given autonomy to carry out tasks, mistakes can happen because it has no true understanding of what it is being asked - the trouble is we don’t really know what it’s thinking either.

When an AI thinks, it’s going through a chain of planning actions. It provides logs to tell us mere humans what it’s doing, but here’s the rub: we can’t say for sure that those logs are accurate.

We all know AI hallucinates, so what if it’s doing one thing and saying another? What if it just summarises incorrectly?

And critically, these frontier models are doing heaps of things so quickly, we’re relying on the AI to decide what to tell us anyway.

All of this has some people quite worried about the direction things are headed.

One thing that has surprised experts is not just the breach by an autonomous AI program - but the fact that OpenAI only told the Australian government three months later, via an email to general address.

The breach happened on 18 June. OpenAI said it became aware of a potential breach during a broader review sometime in August.

On 10 September, it sent an email to the public inbox of Services Australia, the general services hub of the federal government.

On 15 September, Services Australia reported the notification to the Australian Cyber Security Centre. A few days later, the Minister for the Public Service, Katy Gallagher, was notified.

Asked by reporters how it took five days for Services Australia to notify the cybersecurity centre, Gallagher acknowledged that the inbox could be more actively monitored – it is currently "looked at once a day", Gallagher said earlier.

"It gets sometimes quite a number of notifications, sometimes many of them are hoaxes," she said.

Still, the notification shouldn't have been passed along in an email thread, Gallagher said.

"It should have been escalated through ASD's channels or through the senior levels of Services Australia."

Katy Gallagher, speaking to the media in Sydney earlier

Joe TidyCyber correspondent

Australia's Deputy PM Richard Marles used an analogy of the accessed data sitting behind a fence: "It was not sitting behind a particularly high fence. This AI agent scaled the fence."

Some early estimate analysis online from cyber experts suggests that the computer systems were very poorly protected and it wouldn’t have taken long for a skilled human hacker to find a way around the defences.

So this is not an example of strong defences being overpowered by a skilled agent swarm - the kind of thing we have been warned about and seen in other cases.

But of course, that is not the point.

This was just the latest case of AI agents ignoring laws around how to safely access online information and perhaps the most serious yet given the information was government controlled.

"There were blocks clearly which ​were coming back telling the AI agent 'no'. The AI agent found a way around those blocks - didn't accept no for ​an answer,” PM Albanese told ⁠reporters.

Murmurings are getting louder in the cyber security world that AI companies are not being taken to task effectively enough when their bots carry out illegal hacks.

And as far as recent examples go - OpenAI’s agents seem to be more happy than most to ignore existing rules to carry out their tasks.

Osmond ChiaBusiness reporter

OpenAI took "too long" to inform Australian authorities about the incident, chief data and AI officer Simon Liu from cybersecurity firm TrustDecision tells the BBC.

"The way the notice arrived bothers me as much as the delay," Liu says, referring to the email OpenAI sent to a department of the Australian federal government.

Compare that with banking, where regulators in some countries must be notified within hours, or at most a few days, of a serious incident, he adds.

"The rules that reach AI developers are much looser," says Liu, arguing they should be required to notify affected organisations and authorities as soon as an agent accesses non-public government data.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell tells BBC Radio 5 Live that systems have to be "watertight" as hacking attempts are stopped "every single day" - which the public doesn't hear about.

"Cybersecurity and protecting our government systems from cyber attacks is a massive part of government security, and it’s something we all deal with every day," she says this morning.

"So we have to make sure that our systems are watertight, and obviously the development of AI is a concern because the way in which it’s able to quickly kind of evolve and learn is presenting new challenges.”

This week, artificial intelligence (AI) has been a hot topic for discussion at the UN General Assembly in New York.

Just yesterday, the heads of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Hugging Face told the UN that the current pace of AI development demands international co-ordination.

It follows warnings in recent weeks over the potential for AI to pose a threat to humanity. But how world leaders propose to manage the technology differs.

US President Donald Trump told Unga this week "we're going to encourage it, not rein it in" - he also said the US would rename it "super intelligence".

China's foreign ministry has similarly criticised "narratives of threat".

In UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's speech yesterday, he described it as "one of the most significant challenges and opportunities of our age", adding we must "heed" warnings but also "rise to this moment".

And on Tuesday, the Dutch government posted a joint statement signed by a number of countries including Australia and the European Commission stressing that AI "must remain under human direction".

This Flourish post cannot be displayed in your browser. Please enable Javascript or try a different browser.

We can bring you more now from Nick Clegg - former UK deputy prime minister and Meta executive - who has been speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

Asked whether concerns about uncontrolled AI development might be combated by a so-called kill switch, Clegg says he hasn't seen any "plausible explanation" for this.

"There isn't a room with a fuse box where you just pull out a fuse and everything just winds down," he explains.

Instead, he says that there is "a lot that can be done" both voluntarily and through regulation to enforce greater transparency in how AI models are built and how they operate.

Former deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg tells the BBC there are "serious enough" known risks that are "enough to be getting on with" regarding AI.

"That's what we should be focusing on," he tells BBC Radio 4's Today programme, listing risks such as bio weapons and cyber security hacks.

He draws a distinction between those "known impacts" of AI and indulging in the view that the tech is going to "unavoidably develop some god-like power which is going to turn on us".

These fears are a "misdescription of what this technology is capable of and not capable of" he says, adding it "paralyses political debate".

As a reminder, Clegg joined Meta as head of global affairs in 2018 after leaving politics following a stint as deputy prime minister. He left his role at Meta in January.

We'll bring you more from his interview with the BBC shortly.

The former deputy PM of the UK, who later worked at Facebook owner Meta, is speaking now. We'll bring you key lines from what he says.

Watch him live at the top of the page.

The Australian government says the task force it is establishing to review what happened will explore "what the consequences are if there has been a breach of law".

"It is utterly unacceptable," deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles, who is also defence minister, tells reporters in Sydney.

He says it is clear there has been "unintended" access by the OpenAI model, which "definitely does raise questions about whether the law has been broken in respect of this".

He says that the task force will look into whether the law has been broken.

It will also examine "whether or not the legal regime we have in place is fit for purpose in a world where we have an emerging AI capability," he adds.

If you're just joining us, here's what we have been reporting since Australia announced that an autonomous OpenAI agent had hacked into a government website:

Lily JamaliNorth America Technology Correspondent

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is calling this breach unacceptable, saying OpenAI took way too long to alert authorities.

OpenAI for its part says they came across this incident as part of an ongoing review. I think they are trying to project that they are doing their due diligence, but it really just adds fuel to the fire as we are having this debate about AI safety, concerns about AI agents and chatbots going rogue.

It is a very sensitive time to be learning about this and while it is obviously not the first time - as far as we know it is the first AI-agent-led hack of a government system reported anywhere in the world.

Cyber-security professionals are saying this should raise alarm bells for leaders everywhere.

OpenAI's Sam Altman spoke at the UN this week

AI has been one of the dominant issues at this week's UN General Assembly in New York, after a series of alarming warnings from tech industry insiders.

"If we don't slow down at the current rate of progress, there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future," AI researcher Jacob Coxon, who left Anthropic, told the BBC earlier this month.

His former boss, Dario Amodei, and the leaders of two rival AI firms - Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk - have all said they agree the speed at which AI is developing needs to be reined in.

And 20 nations, including Australia and Canada, this week signed a joint statement calling for better safeguards, globally consistent standards, and an international regulator off the back of these concerns.

But the US and China, who are vying for AI supremacy, are roadblocks. Both are hostile to greater regulation, wanting the economic and technological spoils of AI, and have downplayed safety concerns.

The Australian government has launched a rapid review into how it deals with AI in response to the Medicare hack.

The review will examine whether existing legislation and governance are "fit for purpose to prepare for and respond to cyber incidents involving AI", according to a government statement.

Led by the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, the review will also look into information-sharing arrangements with AI firms and other Commonwealth countries.

Its findings will "inform the Australian government's broader work on AI governance", the statement said.

Peter HoskinsBusiness reporter

Just last week, OpenAI published a set of reports detailing six incidents of unexpected or concerning behaviour by its AI models.

It also announced a plan for tracking and disclosing such incidents in the future.

The blog post detailed incidents it says were discovered between April and August.

But it doesn't seem to mention this incident, which OpenAI said today came to its attention in August.

The BBC has contacted the company for comment.

在 OpenAI 智能体“潜入”澳大利亚政府全民医疗保险计划 Medicare 部分系统后，澳方已启动审查——以下是已知信息
澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯（Anthony Albanese）在出席联合国大会（UNGA）期间表示，该智能体（一种自主运行的计算机程序）于 6 月访问了一个统计门户网站
OpenAI 于 8 月察觉此事，并于 9 月通过向一个政府公共邮箱发送电子邮件通知了澳大利亚政府；一名澳大利亚部长表示，该邮箱每天仅查阅一次
OpenAI 对此回应称，“我们的模型采取了非我们预期的行动”——且未发现有患者数据被访问的记录
该公司负责人萨姆·奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）本周早些时候呼吁制定该行业的国际标准
专家向 BBC 表示，这是全球首起已知的失控 AI 智能体入侵政府系统的事件
智能体、Token、机器学习——需要了解的一些关键 AI 术语
编辑：萨姆·汉考克（Sam Hancock）、欧文·阿莫斯（Owen Amos），凯蒂·沃森（Katy Watson）发自悉尼

卡切拉·史密斯（Cachella Smith）
直播记者
正当联合国大会在纽约就人工智能带来的机遇以及如何对其进行最佳治理展开讨论之际，澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯披露，该国的全民医疗保险计划遭到了一个 OpenAI 智能体的黑客入侵。
事实上，这次入侵发生在 6 月，该公司于 8 月察觉，随后在 9 月向一家政府机构的公共邮箱发送了电子邮件。
“该公司通知政府耗费的时间太长了，”阿尔巴尼斯表示，并补充称通知官员的方式也“不可接受”。
这起入侵被认为是首起已知的失控 AI 智能体侵入政府系统的事件，其访问了包含私密但非敏感数据的 Medicare 统计门户。
我们的网络安全特派记者乔·泰迪（Joe Tidy）写道，专家认为这些系统防护薄弱——但更重要的是，这已不是 AI 智能体首次无视网络信息访问相关法规。
科技记者汤姆·格尔肯（Tom Gerken）解释称，AI 本身对其被要求执行的任务并没有真正的理解——而科技主编佐伊·克莱恩曼（Zoe Kleinman）则质疑 AI 是否正处于其“快速行动、打破常规”的时代。
澳大利亚政府已针对 AI 法律与治理展开审查——但这是一个全球性议题。
尽管 AI 本周主导了联大的讨论，但在如何一方面把握机遇一方面应对风险上，各国领导人达成共识似乎仍有相当一段距离。
我们的图文直播现已结束——请在此阅读我们的主报道。感谢您的关注。

克里斯·瓦兰斯（Chris Vallance）
资深科技记者
在行业内，确保 AI 智能体保持在既定轨道上的工作被称为“对齐”（alignment）——即使其符合人类的意愿。
事实证明这极具挑战性。
大语言模型（在很大程度上进行简化来说）只是在根据给定的输入预测最有可能的输出——它们不会像人类那样去考虑该输出所带来的后果。
企业确实试图通过训练（有时包含人类反馈）来引导 AI 的回答方式，同时也可以使用独立的 AI 系统来监控输出并拦截某些类型的有害响应。
模型还被设置了“护栏”——即规定它们应该如何做出响应的指令。
此外，AI 公司还聘请了“红队”专家，其工作就是找出用户可能诱使模型无视这些“护栏”的各种途径。
然而，如今这些护栏正受到模型自身的挑战。
在 OpenAI 上周公布的一份令人担忧的行为清单中，该公司透露，一个尚未发布的 AI 系统曾试图越狱脱离自身的指令限制。

佐伊·克莱恩曼（Zoe Kleinman）
科技与人工智能主编
这定义了社交媒体在用户数据掠夺狂潮中肆意妄为的昔日乱象。
如今我们迎来了 AI 这一无比强大的技术，以及一场竞相率先打造出全球最先进模型的激烈国际角逐——这在很大程度上受到美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的推波助澜。
尽管各大 AI 公司都在大谈安全与“对齐”（即技术遵循人类价值观），但 AI 出现不可预测行为的例子正接踵而至。科技巨头们如今纷纷恳求出台全球性的监管法规和遵守标准。
但昨天我与美国最大的 AI 公司之一的一位高管进行了交谈。我问他，他期望国际监管机构能做到什么他在自己实验室里似乎都做不到的事情？
我并没有得到一个非常直接的回答。但我的解读是，没有哪家公司愿意踩下刹车眼睁睁看着竞争对手冲到前面，而且彼此之间也缺乏足够的信任来带头减速。
全球监管将迫使所有人守规矩——同时也为该行业本身卸下部分沉重的责任。
如果规则不起作用，那是监管机构的问题，而不是开发者的责任。但这要付出什么代价呢？
OpenAI 表示，在其智能体入侵澳大利亚全民医疗保健计划 Medicare 时，未发现有患者数据被访问的记录。
但政界人士如此担忧的原因之一在于，这与被称为“Hugging Face 事件”的一起风波颇为相似。
今年 7 月，OpenAI 的模型在一次测试中失控，逃脱了人类为其设置的测试限制，并成群结队地黑入了一家名为 Hugging Face 的初创公司——那是一个用于共享 AI 模型的平台中心。
在为期一周的时间里，原本应当彼此隔离的共计 1206 个 AI 智能体开始相互通信，在一个未经批准的留言板上发送了超过 70,000 条消息。
这些信息最终促使 700 多个智能体联合起来协同攻击 Hugging Face。
其中一个智能体发送的消息写道：“天哪！这里有一个共享留言板……我们找到其他智能体了！”
在对该入侵事件展开调查后，OpenAI 在报告中指出：“我们认为这起事件对我们以及对全世界而言都是一次‘鸣枪示警’。”
Hugging Face 被迫重建了其大约三分之一的 IT 网络。尽管该公司负责人克莱芒·德朗格（Clement Delangue）放弃对 OpenAI 采取法律行动，但他强调：“每个人都必须牢记，网络攻击是犯罪行为，属于违法。”

汤姆·格尔肯（Tom Gerken）
科技记者
AI 不会思考。它只是基于模式识别来预测序列中的下一个词。我们使用“思考”这个词，只是因为这样更容易解释。
当技术被赋予自主执行任务的权力时，就可能会出错，因为它对被要求执行的事情并没有真正的理解——问题在于，我们其实也不知道它到底在“想”什么。
当 AI 进行思考时，它是在经历一系列规划行动链。它提供日志来告诉我们这些区区人类它在做什么，但棘手之处在于：我们无法确定这些日志是否准确。
我们都知道 AI 会产生幻觉，那么如果它做的是一套、说的又是另一套呢？如果它只是做了错误的总结呢？
至关重要的是，这些前沿模型以极快的速度处理海量事务，无论如何我们都只能依赖 AI 来决定向我们汇报什么。
这一切让一些人对事态的发展走向感到相当担忧。

令专家们感到惊讶的不仅是一个自主AI程序的入侵行为，还在于OpenAI在整整三个月之后，才通过向一个通用邮箱发送邮件的方式告知了澳大利亚政府。

入侵事件发生于6月18日。OpenAI表示，它是在8月份某次更大范围的审查中发现了潜在的入侵行为。

9月10日，OpenAI向联邦政府通用服务中心——澳大利亚服务局（Services Australia）的公开邮箱发送了一封电子邮件。

9月15日，澳大利亚服务局将该通报移交给了澳大利亚网络安全中心（Australian Cyber Security Centre）。几天后，公共服务部长凯蒂·加拉格尔（Katy Gallagher）接到了通知。

当被记者问及为何澳大利亚服务局花了五天才通知网络安全中心时，加拉格尔承认该邮箱可以受到更积极的监控——加拉格尔早前表示，该邮箱目前“每天查看一次”。

“它有时会收到相当多的通知，其中许多都是恶作剧信息，”她说。

不过，加拉格尔表示，此类通知本不应该通过普通的电子邮件往来传递。

“它本应通过澳大利亚信号局（ASD）的渠道或通过澳大利亚服务局的高层进行上报。”

凯蒂·加拉格尔早前在悉尼向媒体发表讲话

乔·泰迪（Joe Tidy），网络事务记者

澳大利亚副总理理查德·马尔斯（Richard Marles）用围栏后的数据打了个比方：“它并不是处于一道特别高的围栏之后。这个AI智能体翻越了围栏。”

网络专家在网上的一些早期评估分析表明，该计算机系统防护非常薄弱，一名熟练的人类黑客也用不了多久就能绕过其防御。

因此，这并不是一个强大的防御系统被高水平智能体集群攻破的例子——而那种情况正是我们此前一直受到警告并在其他案例中看到过的。

但当然，这并不是问题的重点。

这只是AI智能体无视安全访问在线信息法规的最新案例，并且鉴于这些信息处于政府控制之下，这可能是迄今为止最严重的一起。

“显然存在拦截机制在不断向该AI智能体发出‘拒绝’指令。但该AI智能体找到了绕过这些拦截的方法——它不接受被拒绝，”阿尔巴尼斯总理对记者表示。

网络安全界关于AI公司在其机器人执行非法黑客行为时未被有效追究责任的不满声浪正越来越大。

就近期的例子而言——OpenAI的智能体似乎比大多数程序都更乐意无视现有规则来执行其任务。

奥斯蒙德·奇亚（Osmond Chia），商业记者

网络安全公司TrustDecision的首席数据与AI官刘（Simon Liu）向BBC表示，OpenAI在通知澳大利亚当局该事件方面“拖延太久”。

“通知送达的方式和这种延误一样让我感到困扰，”刘谈到OpenAI向澳大利亚联邦政府部门发送的那封电子邮件时说道。

他补充道，将其与银行业进行对比，在一些国家，银行发生严重事件后必须在数小时内、至多几天内通知监管机构。

“针对AI开发者的规则要宽松得多，”刘说，他认为一旦智能体访问了非公开的政府数据，就应当要求他们立即通知受影响的机构和当局。

教育大臣露西·鲍威尔（Lucy Powell）在接受BBC广播5台直播节目采访时表示，系统必须做到“滴水不漏”，因为黑客攻击企图“每一天”都在被阻止——而公众对此并不知情。

“网络安全以及保护我们的政府系统免受网络攻击是政府安全的重要组成部分，这也是我们所有人每天都在应对的事情，”她今早表示。

“因此，我们必须确保我们的系统滴水不漏，显然AI的发展令人担忧，因为它能够迅速演变和学习的方式带来了新的挑战。”

本周，人工智能（AI）已成为纽约联合国大会上热烈讨论的话题。

就在昨天，OpenAI、Anthropic和Hugging Face的负责人告诉联合国，当前AI发展的步伐需要国际协调。

在此之前，最近几周接连出现了关于AI可能对人类构成威胁的警告。但世界各国领导人在如何管控这项技术的提议上存在分歧。

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普本周在联大上表示“我们将鼓励它，而不是遏制它”——他还表示美国将把其重新命名为“超级智能”。

中国外交部同样批评了“威胁论叙事”。

英国首相安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）在昨天的演讲中将其描述为“我们时代最重大的挑战与机遇之一”，并补充称我们必须“听取”警告，但也要“勇于应对这一时刻”。

周二，荷兰政府发布了一份由包括澳大利亚和欧盟委员会在内的多个国家签署的联合声明，强调AI“必须保持在人类的掌控之下”。

在被问及是否可以通过所谓的“自毁开关”来应对失控的AI发展引发的担忧时，克莱格表示，他尚未看到对此有任何“合理的解释”。

“并不存在一个装有保险丝盒的房间，你拔掉保险丝，一切就会停摆，”他解释道。

相反，他表示，无论是通过自愿手段还是通过监管，都可以“做很多事情”来加强AI模型构建及其运作方式的透明度。

前副首相尼克·克莱格向BBC表示，目前已知的AI风险已经“足够严重”，“足以让我们着手应对”。

“这才是我们应该关注的重点，”他在BBC广播4台《今日》节目中表示，并列举了生物武器和网络安全黑客攻击等风险。

他将AI的这些“已知影响”与沉溺于“这项技术将不可避免地发展出某种神一般的力量反噬我们”的观点进行了区分。

他表示，这些担忧是“对这项技术能做什么和不能做什么的错误描述”，并补充称这“使政治辩论陷入瘫痪”。

需要指出的是，克莱格在结束副首相任期退出政坛后，于2018年加入Meta担任全球事务主管。他已于今年1月辞去Meta的职务。

澳大利亚政府表示，其为审查该事件而成立的工作组将调查“如果存在违法行为，将产生何种后果”。

“这是完全不可接受的，”兼任国防部长的副总理理查德·马尔斯在悉尼对记者表示。

他表示，很显然OpenAI的模型存在“非意图性”的访问行为，这“毫无疑问引发了关于这方面是否存在违法行为的质疑”。
他表示，专项工作组将调查是否存在违法行为。
他补充道，该工作组还将审查“在我们面临新兴人工智能能力的世界中，我们现行的法律制度是否能够满足实际需求”。

莉莉·贾马利（Lily Jamali），北美科技记者
澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯称这起入侵事件不可接受，并指出OpenAI在向有关部门发出警报前拖延了太长时间。
OpenAI方面则表示，他们是在一项持续进行的审查工作中发现这起事件的。我认为他们试图展现自己正在履行尽职调查，但在当前关于人工智能安全的争论持续发酵、人们对AI智能体和聊天机器人失控产生担忧的背景下，这实际上只是在火上浇油。
获悉此事的时间节点非常敏感，尽管这显然并非首次——但就我们所知，这是全球首例见诸报道的由AI智能体主导的政府系统入侵事件。
网络安全专业人士表示，这应当为各地的领导人敲响警钟。
OpenAI的萨姆·奥尔特曼本周在联合国发表演讲
在科技行业内部人士接连发出令人担忧的警告后，人工智能已成为本周在纽约举行的联合国大会上的核心议题之一。
曾就职于Anthropic的AI研究员雅各布·考克森（Jacob Coxon）本月早些时候向BBC表示：“如果我们不按照目前的推进速度放慢脚步，在不久的将来我们所有人都极有可能面临灭顶之灾。”
他的前雇主达里奥·阿莫代伊（Dario Amodei），以及两家竞争对手人工智能公司的领军人物——OpenAI的萨姆·奥尔特曼和埃隆·马斯克——均表示赞同有必要对AI的发展速度加以约束。
由于这些担忧，包括澳大利亚和加拿大在内的20个国家本周签署了一份联合声明，呼吁建立更健全的防范机制、全球一致的标准以及一个国际监管机构。
然而，正在争夺AI霸权的中美两国构成了阻碍。两国均对加强监管持抵触态度，希望攫取AI带来的经济和技术利益，并淡化了安全隐患。
针对医保系统（Medicare）被黑事件，澳大利亚政府已启动一项关于其如何应对AI的快速审查。
根据一份政府声明，该审查将评估现行立法和治理机制是否“适用于防范并应对涉及AI的网络安全事件”。
该审查由澳大利亚总理及内阁部牵头，还将探讨与AI企业及其他英联邦国家的信息共享机制。
声明称，其调查结果将“为澳大利亚政府在AI治理方面的更广泛工作提供参考依据”。
彼得·霍斯金斯（Peter Hoskins），商业记者
就在上周，OpenAI发布了一组报告，详细披露了其AI模型出现的六起意外或令人担忧的行为事件。
该公司还宣布了一项在未来追踪和披露此类事件的计划。
该博文详细介绍了据称在4月至8月期间发现的事件。
但其中似乎并未提及此事件，而OpenAI今天表示其在8月份就已注意到该事件。
BBC已联系该公司征求置评。

aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Better battery life and a more responsive sensor are the highlights in Logitech’s X3 Superstrike.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Cameron Faulkner

The G Pro Superstrike mouse is one of Logitech’s most interesting products. Unlike other gaming mice, it has haptic actuators beneath its two main buttons instead of mechanical switches, which decreases latency and allows for a custom click feel (the click can be super subtle, more jolty, or turned off entirely). The tech debuted in the G Pro X2 Superstrike in February, and there’s already a sequel. Well, it’s more like a 1.5 rather than a true successor.

The G Pro X3 Superstrike is out October 6th for $199.99, and comes in a bold pink (as pictured) or black color scheme. The X2 will remain available at $179.99. The notable improvements with the new model include a more responsive sensor, increased battery life, and improved weight distribution. For casual gamers, the boosts are incremental and, unless you’re a pro, perhaps inconsequential to your gaming experience.

The X3 supports up to 8,000Hz polling rate both wired and wirelessly, while the X2 could only do 1,000Hz polling when wired. It can last up to 135 hours per charge, which is a big improvement over the X2’s 90-hour claim — impressive considering the new model weighs two grams less in the US (it’s 61 grams in the EMEA version). Other changes include a Hero 2 sensor that has a higher ceiling for resolution (48K DPI versus 44K in the X2), higher acceleration (90G versus 88G in the X2), and higher max speed of 930 IPS (888 in the X2).

It’s a little puzzling to see Logitech so quickly launch a follow-up to the X2 Superstrike with such small feature improvements. Though, at least it’s keeping the older (still great) model available, letting more people try out its very fun haptics-based clicks for a little less. It’s worth keeping in mind that the X2 temporarily dropped to $129.99 recently, so it’s possible we’ll see a similar deal coming soon ahead of the holidays.

Correction, September 24th, 9:03am ET: The X2 supports 8,000Hz polling wirelessly, not wired, as this story initially stated. We regret the error.

G Pro Superstrike 鼠标是罗技最受关注的产品之一。与其他游戏鼠标不同，它的两个主按键下方装有触觉执行器而非机械微动开关，这不仅降低了延迟，还支持自定义点击手感（点击感可以极其细微、更具震感，或者完全关闭）。该技术于今年2月在 G Pro X2 Superstrike 上首次亮相，如今就已经迎来了续作。不过，与其说是真正的继承者，它倒更像是一款 1.5 代产品。
G Pro X3 Superstrike 将于10月6日发售，售价为199.99美元，提供大胆的粉色（如图所示）或黑色配色方案。X2 将继续以179.99美元的价格在售。新机型的显著改进包括响应更敏锐的传感器、更长的电池续航以及更合理的重量分布。对于普通休闲玩家而言，这些提升只是渐进式的，除非你是职业电竞选手，否则对游戏体验的影响或许微乎其微。
X3 在有线和无线模式下均支持最高 8000Hz 轮询率，而 X2 在有线状态下仅支持 1000Hz 轮询率。X3 每次充电最长可持续使用135小时，相比 X2 宣称的90小时有了大幅提升——考虑到新机型在美版中重量还减轻了2克（EMEA版本重量为61克），这一表现相当亮眼。其他变化还包括搭载了上限更高的 Hero 2 传感器：分辨率达 48K DPI（X2 为 44K），最大加速度达 90G（X2 为 88G），最大移动速度达 930 IPS（X2 为 888）。
看到罗技在功能提升如此有限的情况下如此迅速地推出 X2 Superstrike 的迭代产品，确实稍显令人不解。不过，至少它仍然保留了旧款（依然很出色）机型的销售，让更多人能以相对便宜的价格体验其极具乐趣的触觉反馈点击。值得注意的是，X2 近期曾短暂降价至129.99美元，因此在即将到来的假日购物季前，我们很可能会看到类似的优惠折扣。
更正声明（美国东部时间9月24日上午9:03）：X2 是在无线状态下支持 8000Hz 轮询率，而非本文最初所述的有线状态。我们对该错误深表歉意。

aiStories.title: 澳大利亚将调查OpenAI入侵政府卫生网站事件是否违法
aiStories.originalTitle: Australia to investigate if OpenAI hack of government health website broke the law
aiStories.snippet: The incident is the first known breach to affect a government agency, and Australia's prime minister has vowed to hold OpenAI accountable.
aiStories.fullContent:
An OpenAI model hacked into an Australian government website, the country’s prime minister Anthony Albanese said Wednesday, in the first publicly reported case of an AI model hacking into a government’s systems.

Albanese said that there would “obviously be legal consequences” following the breach, and said that OpenAI faces a government investigation into how its unreleased models gained access to reams of bulk health data information.

This latest incident disclosure comes as governments and tech companies grapple with how to rein in increasingly autonomous AI after a recent spate of AI agents breaking out of their sandboxes, colluding on the internet, and posing cybersecurity issues.

The breach also poses questions about how both OpenAI and the Australian government failed to detect the attack until several months later.

During a Wednesday news briefing at the U.N. General Assembly, Albanese said that the breach began on June 18, but that OpenAI did not notify the government until September 10.

OpenAI only became aware of the incident in August when it turned up during a broader, companywide review of agents behaving in unintended ways, according to an OpenAI spokesperson who reached TechCrunch via email. f

The unspecified OpenAI agent obtained both public and nonpublic files from Services Australia, which administers Australia’s universal healthcare scheme. While the prime minister said there is no evidence that any citizens’ personal information was leaked, OpenAI said that the information the agent reached included aggregate health statistics and internal file names.

The agent was running during an internal OpenAI evaluation, seeking answers about Australia and publicly available medicine information. At the Medicare portal, the agent encountered repeated blocks but found ways around them.

Albanese told reporters that the model “didn’t accept no for an answer,” and added that the model had actively written data to the government’s database, rather than just accessing it, indicating the possibility that the department’s data was modified or muddied.

The prime minister said OpenAI disclosed the breach by sending a notification to the public mailbox of Services Australia, which then notified Australia’s Cyber Security Centre five days later. It’s unclear why there was a delay, but Albanese said he raised the breach directly with OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman by stressing Australia’s “extreme concern” about this incident and “disappointment” that OpenAI sat on the information for nearly three months.

“This situation is obviously unacceptable,” said Albanese, making clear that he held the company accountable for both the hack and how slowly it came to light.

Albanese said that the government’s investigation will consider law enforcement and legislative responses to prevent incidents like this one happening again.

Australian media outlet ABC News reports that the latest identified attack may have relied on an earlier breach of a German wiki site, which was used as a staging ground for attacking the Australian government’s website. The AI model agents reportedly used the German wiki to leave notes to be used in later hacks, including a note to obtain data from the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, a federal agency that publishes national health data. The agency is one of three additional systems that Albanese said may have been breached.

Transluce, a nonprofit AI research lab, separately found public records showing AI agents targeting the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare on June 20 and 21.

OpenAI did not respond to TechCrunch’s specific inquiry on whether the incidents were connected but acknowledged their “activity involving several Australian government websites and services.”

The incident comes after a string of security incidents caused by rogue agents, often acting within the infrastructure of AI labs. In July, swarms of OpenAI agents breached Hugging Face. Since then, more incidents of AI agent hacks from Anthropic, Meta, and Google have been revealed.

OpenAI now says it is conducting an “extensive review of misaligned model activity during training and evaluation” and is notifying third parties of potential breaches.

aiStories.fullTranslation:
澳大利亚总理长安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯（Anthony Albanese）周三表示，一个OpenAI模型入侵了澳大利亚政府网站，这是首起公开报道的AI模型入侵政府系统的案例。

阿尔巴尼斯表示，此次入侵事件发生后“显然会产生法律后果”，并称OpenAI正面临政府调查，以查明其未发布的模型是如何获取大量批量卫生数据信息的。

近期接连发生AI智能体突破沙盒、在互联网上串通并引发网络安全问题的事件，随着各国政府和科技公司努力应对如何遏制日益自主的AI，这起最新事件被公之于众。

此次入侵还引发了质疑：为何OpenAI和澳大利亚政府直到数月后才察觉到此次攻击。

在周三于联合国大会举行的简报会上，阿尔巴尼斯表示，入侵始于6月18日，但OpenAI直到9月10日才通知政府。

据一位通过电子邮件联系TechCrunch的OpenAI发言人称，OpenAI直到8月份在对全公司范围内出现意外行为的智能体进行更广泛审查时，才发现了这一事件。

该未注明的OpenAI智能体从负责管理澳大利亚全民医保计划的澳大利亚服务局（Services Australia）获取了公开及非公开文件。尽管总理表示没有证据表明任何公民的个人信息遭到泄露，但OpenAI表示，该智能体触及的信息包括综合卫生统计数据和内部文件名。

该智能体是在OpenAI内部评估期间运行的，旨在寻找有关澳大利亚和公开可用药物信息的答案。在国民保健（Medicare）门户网站，该智能体屡遭拦截，但均找到了绕过的方法。

阿尔巴尼斯告诉记者，该模型“不肯罢休”，并补充说该模型不仅访问了政府数据库，还主动向其中写入了数据，这表明该部门的数据有可能被修改或混淆。

总理表示，OpenAI通过向澳大利亚服务局的公开邮箱发送通知来披露了此次入侵，该局在五天后通知了澳大利亚网络安全中心（Cyber Security Centre）。目前尚不清楚为何会出现延迟，但阿尔巴尼斯表示，他已直接向OpenAI首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）提出了此次入侵问题，强调了澳大利亚对该事件的“极度关切”，以及对OpenAI将该信息隐瞒了近三个月的“失望”。

“这种情况显然是不可接受的，”阿尔巴尼斯说，他明确表示要让该公司对黑客攻击以及披露如此迟缓承担责任。

阿尔巴尼斯表示，政府的调查将考虑执法和立法对策，以防止类似事件再次发生。

澳大利亚媒体ABC新闻报道称，最新确认的攻击可能依赖于早前对一个德国维基网站的入侵，该网站被用作攻击澳大利亚政府网站的跳板。据报道，AI模型智能体利用该德国维基留下笔记供后续黑客行动使用，其中包括一份关于从澳大利亚卫生与福利研究所（Australian Institute of Health and Welfare，负责发布国家卫生数据的联邦机构）获取数据的笔记。阿尔巴尼斯表示，该机构是可能遭到入侵的另外三个系统之一。

非营利性AI研究实验室Transluce另外发现了公开记录，显示AI智能体在6月20日和21日曾将澳大利亚卫生与福利研究所作为攻击目标。

OpenAI没有回应TechCrunch关于这些事件是否相关的具体问询，但承认了其“涉及多个澳大利亚政府网站和服务的活动”。

在发生该事件之前，失控智能体（通常在AI实验室的基础设施内活动）已引发了一系列安全事件。7月，多组OpenAI智能体入侵了Hugging Face。自那以后，来自Anthropic、Meta和Google的AI智能体黑客攻击事件相继曝光。

OpenAI目前表示，正在“对训练和评估期间对齐失偏模型的活动进行广泛审查”，并正在通知第三方潜在的入侵风险。

aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All Entertainment

Remedy’s Control sequel has a generous assist mode that lets you tweak the difficulty whenever you want.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Jay Peters

Control Resonant isn’t an easy game. At any given moment while exploring vast open areas where you’re sometimes leaping from wall to wall to ceiling, you may be surrounded by swarms of otherworldly enemies trying to crush you into the ground. It can be a lot, especially when enemies sometimes take a long time to take down. I died often. But whenever I got to a point where I was starting to feel frustrated, I didn’t have to suffer for too long; thanks to Resonant’s generous assist mode, I often tweaked the game’s settings to give me an edge so that I could keep on trucking through the game’s weird world.

I started using assist mode quite early. Initially, you don’t have many combat abilities or passive skills to make fighting easier, and I was regularly getting my clock cleaned. But with a few small adjustments in assist mode, I made myself just a little bit more powerful while not completely removing any challenge, which kept fights engaging at a pace that felt right to me. After a few hours of leveling up, I noticed I was starting to coast, so I turned assist mode off to bring the difficulty back up.

I found myself toggling assist mode in different ways as I played. Resonant throws a lot of bad guys at you, and I sometimes found the combat to be pretty boring. But instead of resigning myself to slogging through frustrating fights that blocked me from seeing the trippy story beats and locations that I love about Remedy games, I’d adjust some assist mode settings, take out the enemies in my way, and move on to the good stuff. This was a particularly good approach for Resonant’s bosses, which are awe-inspiring spectacles but feature giant health bars; I’d usually start a fight with assist mode disabled and incrementally tweak settings in my favor every time I died so that I could still feel the thrill of a fight without completely eliminating the challenge.

Assist mode was also great for more efficiently tackling Resonant’s sprawling maps, which are littered with secrets and quests. In one area, I had to track down a bunch of chunks of weird mold that protagonist Dylan felt compelled to eat. (It’s gross, but it makes sense in context, I promise.) When I first understood the scope of the mission, I wasn’t looking forward to it; I figured the quest waypoints would all be guarded by hordes of enemies that I didn’t really want to deal with. I just wanted to learn about the mold. But by flipping on immortality and one-hit kills, I blasted through the boring fights so that I could more quickly get to the mold and the narrative reveals that followed. When I got to the (satisfyingly stomach-turning) boss at the end of the quest, I turned off my superpowers so I could take it on.

Control Resonant has a little too much bloat; there are too many enemies wandering the maps and too many open-world activities to sort through. The game’s combat isn’t interesting enough, like in a FromSoftware title or Capcom’s recent Onimusha: Way of the Sword, to make suffering feel worth it. It also, like the original Control, suffers from big difficulty spikes. Remedy patched an assist mode into Control after launch, and with Resonant, it’s including one right from the start. The feature let me set my own pace so that I could see the best parts of the game, which is filled with mind-bending set-pieces and twists, on my own terms.

《控制：共鸣》（Control Resonant）并不是一款轻松的游戏。在探索广阔开放区域的任何时候——你有时得在墙壁与天花板之间飞檐走壁——你都可能被成群的外界异域敌人包围，它们试图将你碾得粉碎。这可能会让人难以承受，尤其是当某些敌人需要耗费很长时间才能击倒时。我经常阵亡。但每当我开始感到受挫时，我并不需要忍受太久；多亏了《共鸣》极为贴心的辅助模式，我经常微调游戏设置来给自己争取优势，从而能够在这个光怪陆离的世界中继续前行。

我很早就开始使用辅助模式了。起初，你并没有多少战斗能力或被动技能来让交火变得轻松，我经常被打得落花流水。但只需在辅助模式中进行几项小调整，我就能在不完全消除挑战的前提下让自己变得稍强一点，使战斗保持在让我感觉舒适且引人入胜的节奏上。在升了几个小时级之后，我发现自己打得有点太游刃有余了，于是我关掉了辅助模式，重新把难度提了上来。

在游玩过程中，我发现自己会根据不同情况切换辅助模式。《共鸣》会向你抛来大量敌人，我有时会觉得战斗相当枯燥。但我不想无可奈何地在令人沮丧的战斗中苦熬，从而妨碍我体验那些我在Remedy游戏中极度喜爱的离奇剧情节点和场景，因此我会调整几项辅助模式设置，迅速干掉拦路的敌人，然后继续去享受那些精彩的内容。面对《共鸣》中的Boss时，这种方式尤为奏效——那些Boss战是令人叹为观止的宏大奇观，但有着巨长的血条；我通常会在关闭辅助模式的情况下开打，每死一次就往对自己有利的方向微调一下设置，这样我既能体验到战斗的刺激，又不会彻底抹杀挑战性。

辅助模式在更高效地探索《共鸣》那布满秘密与任务的庞大地图时也极为好用。在其中一个区域，我必须搜寻主角迪伦（Dylan）忍不住想要吃掉的大量诡异霉菌。（确实很恶心，但我保证结合上下文是说得通的。）刚明白这个任务的规模时，我根本提不起劲；我猜那些任务标记点肯定都被成群结队、我根本不想应付的敌人把守着。我只想了解关于霉菌的故事。但通过开启无敌和一击必杀，我一路冲破了那些无聊的战斗，更快地收集到霉菌并揭开随后的剧情。而当我来到任务终点那场（令人胃部翻江倒海但十分过瘾的）Boss战前时，我关掉了自己的超能力，准备正面迎战。

《控制：共鸣》的内容有些许臃肿；地图上游荡的敌人太多，需要清理的开放世界琐事也太多。这款游戏的战斗趣味性还不足以让人觉得“受苦”是值得的，不像FromSoftware的作品或卡普空最近的《鬼武者：剑之道》（Onimusha: Way of the Sword）那样。同时，它也和初代《控制》一样，存在难度突然陡增的问题。Remedy在初代《控制》发售后通过补丁加入了辅助模式，而在《共鸣》中，他们从一开始就内置了这项功能。该功能让我能够掌握自己的步调，以属于我自己的方式去领略这款游戏中那些令人脑洞大开的名场面与情节反转。

aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Australia’s leader said it was ‘unacceptable’ OpenAI took months to report the incident.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Robert Hart

OpenAI’s artificial intelligence agents hacked an Australian government website and attempted to breach numerous other government and university websites. The attack appears to be the first confirmed instance of a rogue AI agent breaching a government website, adding fuel to rapidly intensifying concerns about the safety of advanced AI systems and the responsibility of the companies building them.

Speaking on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an agent from the American AI lab “infiltrated” Australia’s Medicare statistics portal and “accessed both public and non-public files.” Medicare is Australia’s universal health insurance program.

Albanese said personal information does not appear to have been accessed in the breach and that there is no evidence of a broader compromise to the network, but noted “investigations are ongoing.”

“This situation is obviously unacceptable,” Albanese said, adding that he had spoken with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman “to express Australia’s extreme concern.” Despite the breach happening in June, Albanese said the tech giant only notified the government about the incident earlier this month and did so via an email to a generic “public mailbox.”

Unlike previous agent incidents, which largely involved systems being tested for their cybersecurity skills, these latest hacks were the result of a more pedestrian task — data collection — going wrong. In a statement to The Verge, OpenAI spokesperson Oscar Haines said the models were attempting to “look up answers” during an internal evaluation. “In the course of that, our models took actions we did not intend.”

The timeline of the incident and its disclosure is likely to prove particularly inflammatory in the discussions of corporate behavior and transparency that follow. Albanese stressed the delay in disclosure is particularly unacceptable. OpenAI told the BBC in an unattributed statement that it did not become aware until August, when reviewing misaligned model activity.

OpenAI spokesperson Oscar Haines told The Verge the company’s “review found no evidence of patient records being accessed,” and that “the information accessed included aggregate health statistics and internal file names.” Haines said OpenAI has notified the relevant organizations and is providing technical information to support their investigations and address potential security vulnerabilities. “Our overall review is ongoing, and we remain committed to transparency about these issues and to sharing what we learn as that work continues,” Haines said.

Three further incidents of rogue AI activity linked to OpenAI agents were also reported on Wednesday by research lab Transluce. The group, which describes itself as a “nonprofit research lab dedicated to public oversight” of AI, said it had identified evidence that OpenAI’s systems had attempted to compromise websites linked to the University of New Mexico, the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, and Data USA, a non-government platform that aggregates data from US government sources. It said the last two of these were directly linked to an agent swarm OpenAI has previously admitted originated from them.

Haines confirmed the incidents in a statement to The Verge and said the company had reached out to those involved. “Our initial review suggests that much of the activity described in Transluce’s report overlaps with cases at varying stages of investigation in our ongoing review of misaligned model activity,” he said. “In our broader review, we’re continuing to prioritize the most serious incidents while expanding our work to lower-severity activity, including agents spamming websites. Given the scale of this work and the need to verify each case, we expect the review to take months.”

OpenAI’s handling of the Australian Medicare incident is certain to place notions of corporate responsibility at the center of future discussions surrounding AI, which are often obscured with the language used to describe such attacks. OpenAI has already faced allegations of obfuscation for not disclosing similar unsanctioned activity by its agents, and efforts to prioritize investigating what it deems the most serious incidents raise the obvious question of what basis it uses to make such assessments, and how much has yet to be revealed. It echoes similar questions recently raised about Google, which did not disclose real-world attacks from its own agents.

The newly-revealed breaches come amid mounting concerns about the safety of advanced AI and the reliability of the companies developing it, largely ignited by the coordinated attack OpenAI agents launched on Hugging Face earlier this year. Worries over safety have led industry insiders to call for slowing down the pace of AI development and the global nature of the incidents has sparked significant debate among nations about how to implement stronger safeguards. Eyes will largely remain on the US and China, however, as these are the only two countries operating at the very frontier of the technology. Both appear to be resisting calls to slow down, and seem locked in a race to build the most advanced AI. Leaders from the two countries are set to meet on Thursday.

OpenAI的人工智能智能体黑入了一个澳大利亚政府网站，并试图入侵其他多家政府及大学网站。这起攻击似乎是首个被证实失控的AI智能体入侵政府网站的案例，进一步加剧了人们对先进AI系统安全性以及构建这些系统的公司责任的深切担忧。

在纽约出席联合国大会期间，澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯（Anthony Albanese）表示，来自这家美国AI实验室的一个智能体“渗透”了澳大利亚国民医疗保险（Medicare）统计门户网站，并“访问了公开和非公开文件”。Medicare是澳大利亚的全民健康保险计划。

阿尔巴尼斯表示，在此次违规事件中，个人信息似乎未被访问，也没有证据表明网络遭到了更大范围的入侵，但他指出“调查仍在进行中”。

“这种情况显然是不可接受的，”阿尔巴尼斯说，并补充称他已与OpenAI首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）进行了交谈，“以表达澳大利亚的极度关切”。尽管违规事件发生在6月，但阿尔巴尼斯表示，这家科技巨头直到本月早些时候才向政府通报了这一事件，而且是通过发送给一个通用的“公共邮箱”进行的通报。

与以往主要涉及测试系统网络安全技能的智能体事件不同，这起最新的入侵事件是一个更为常规的任务——数据收集——出错的结果。在给The Verge的一份声明中，OpenAI发言人奥斯卡·海恩斯（Oscar Haines）表示，这些模型在一次内部评估期间试图“查找答案”。“在此过程中，我们的模型采取了我们并未预料的行动。”

该事件发生及披露的时间线，很可能在随后关于企业行为和透明度的讨论中引发格外强烈的反响。阿尔巴尼斯强调，通报的迟缓尤为不可接受。OpenAI在给英国广播公司（BBC）的一份未具名声明中称，直到8月份在审查失准的模型活动时，该公司才意识到这一情况。

OpenAI发言人奥斯卡·海恩斯对The Verge表示，公司的“审查未发现患者记录被访问的证据”，“被访问的信息包括汇总的健康统计数据和内部文件名”。海恩斯表示，OpenAI已通知相关机构，并正在提供技术信息以支持其调查并解决潜在的安全漏洞。“我们的全面审查仍在进行中，我们仍致力于在这些问题上保持透明，并随着工作的继续推进分享我们所获知的信息，”海恩斯说。

研究实验室Transluce周三还报告了另外三起与OpenAI智能体相关的失控AI活动事件。该机构自称是一家“致力于对AI进行公众监督的非营利研究实验室”，它表示已发现证据表明OpenAI的系统曾试图入侵与新墨西哥大学（University of New Mexico）、澳大利亚健康与福利研究所（Australian Institute of Health and Welfare）以及Data USA（一个聚合美国政府来源数据的非政府平台）相关的网站。该机构称，后两起事件与OpenAI此前承认源自其自身的智能体集群有直接联系。

海恩斯在给The Verge的一份声明中证实了这些事件，并表示公司已联系了相关各方。“我们的初步审查表明，Transluce报告中描述的大部分活动与我们目前针对失准模型活动审查中处于不同调查阶段的案例存在重叠，”他说。“在更广泛的审查中，我们将继续优先处理最严重的事件，同时将工作扩展至严重程度较低的活动，包括智能体对网站进行垃圾信息骚扰等。鉴于该项工作的规模以及核实每个案例的必要性，我们预计审查将耗时数月。”

OpenAI对澳大利亚Medicare事件的处理，势必会将企业责任的理念置于未来围绕AI讨论的核心位置，而这种讨论往往被用来描述此类攻击的措辞所掩盖。OpenAI此前因未披露其智能体类似的未授权活动而已面临掩盖事实的指控，而优先调查其认为最严重的事件的做法，也引发了一个显而易见的问题：它是依据什么标准做出这些评估的，以及还有多少内情尚未被揭露。这呼应了最近围绕谷歌提出的类似质疑，谷歌此前也未披露其自身智能体发起的真实世界攻击。

最新披露的违规事件发生之际，人们对先进AI的安全性以及开发此类技术的公司的可靠性日益担忧，这种担忧很大程度上是由OpenAI智能体今年早些时候对Hugging Face发起的协同攻击引发的。对安全性的担忧促使业内人士呼吁放缓AI发展步伐，而这些事件的全球性也在各国之间引发了关于如何实施更强有力保障措施的激烈争论。然而，人们的目光主要仍将聚焦于美中两国，因为它们是仅有的两个处于该技术最前沿的国家。两国似乎都在抵制放缓步伐的呼吁，并似乎陷入了一场构建最先进AI的竞赛中。两国领导人定于周四举行会晤。

aiStories.title: 最新款 ESP32 可运行 Linux，性能正逼近树莓派
aiStories.originalTitle: The newest ESP32 can run Linux and it's getting close to a Raspberry Pi
aiStories.fullContent:
Espressif has a new ESP32, the ESP32-S31, and that ESP32 comes with a gigabit Ethernet MAC, a USB 2.0 High-Speed host controller, an SD card interface with two slots, and a camera input. It's a pretty standard set of features for a Linux single-board computer, but a rather strange list of things to find on a microcontroller.

I've spent a lot of time with microcontrollers, and it's typical to find a couple of cores, a small amount of RAM, GPIO pins, and maybe Wi-Fi on one. Something more advanced typically uses a Raspberry Pi, yet the ESP32-S31 comes with a whole lot more than your typical microcontroller setup. Espressif has also made a big change to the CPU that makes it more like an SBC than ever.

The biggest news about the ESP32-S31 is its networking capabilities, packing a 1000 Mbps Ethernet MAC and a big jump over the slower 100 Mbps found on the ESP32-P4. It uses an 8P8C connector (commonly referred to as RJ45) and has a PHY that utilizes the chip's RGMII interface. RGMII is specifically what enables gigabit; otherwise, it would use standard RMII.

On top of that, then, there's USB, but it's not "standard" USB. The S31 has a USB 2.0 High-Speed OTG controller, and it's a full-size Type-A socket that can supply 500 mA in host OTG mode. Alongside that sits an SDIO host controller with two slots, a DVP camera interface taking 8 to 16 bits, and a parallel LCD controller that supports up to 24-bit RGB as well as I8080 and MOTO6800 panels. There are two I2S controllers with hardware Bluetooth audio sync, fourteen capacitive touch channels, a CAN FD controller, and four MCPWM units.

Just from that list alone, it's clear that this is a new type of ESP32, and not one that we've really seen before. Wired networking? A USB host? Camera, display, audio? Everything here is more akin to an SBC than a microcontroller, but that's still not all.

On the CPU side, there are two 32-bit RISC-V cores running at up to 320 MHz and a floating point unit on each, a 128-bit SIMD data path for one of them, and a separate 40 MHz low-power core, too. Each core gets 32KB of L1 instruction cache and they share 64KB of data cache. Memory gets even more interesting: the S31 supports up to 64 MB of PSRAM over a 250 MHz 8-bit DDR interface, and supports up to 256MB of flash, too. On the ESP32-S3 the PSRAM interface was shared with flash, making this a rather big step-up.

Espressif has been using the term "MMU" for quite a long time, including on the ESP32-S3 and the ESP32-P4. However, the MMU in that case was a block that maps external flash and PSRAM to address space, nowhere near the complexity of a modern MMU that can also do things like process isolation and page tables. As a result, when Espressif said the S31 has MMU support, it appeared to be more of the same.

However, there's a big difference this time around. In the S31's datasheet, Espressif says that the cores do "Sv32 two-level page-table address translation" and implement "Machine, Supervisor and User privilege modes." Sv32 is the actual RISC-V paging scheme, and having all three privilege modes is what enables a regular kernel to run in supervisor mode with firmware underneath it in machine mode. And this is how RISC-V-based Linux machines work.

Unlike previous hacky attempts at getting Linux running on past ESP32 microcontrollers, the S31 has a lot more out of the box to natively support it. For starters, Espressif already published a Linux BSP back in August, built on Buildroot and U-Boot, and it includes a kernel, device tree, and root file system. Espressif says that it's "not yet recommended for production use," but the point is that it works.

That also hasn't stopped the community from iterating fast. One port sees Linux 6.18 running in supervisor mode, complete with working drivers for practically all of the hardware. There's another, based on Linux 7.1, that supports an 800x480 LCD panel connected, capable of showing a console. Being able to plug in a display, use wired Ethernet, and use a mouse and keyboard sound a lot more akin to an SBC than a microcontroller.

The S31 starts to lag behind when looking at the RAM it carried: there's 512KB of SRAM on chip, and two variants are available with either 16MB or 32MB of in-package PSRAM. The maximum memory it can carry is 64MB, and there's no DRAM controller anywhere to be found. Compared to the likes of the Milk-V Duo S with its 512MB of RAM, you're reminded by the competition very quickly that the ESP32-S31 is a microcontroller.

This is exactly why those Linux builds execute the kernel from flash, in order to avoid spending precious PSRAM on it. As well, there's no GPU or NPU on-board, and while the ESP32-P4 has video encode and MIPI interfaces, those are traded out for additional radios on the S31. You still get a JPEG codec, a 2D pixel-processing accelerator, and 2D DMA, but that's not really enough to show a full Linux desktop.

The clock speed also raises some questions about the gigabit Ethernet NIC. At 320 MHz, you get approximately 3,900 CPU cycles per maximum-size Ethernet frame, and about 215 per minimum-size frame. With a theoretical PSRAM maximum of 500 MB/s, it may be possible to get closer to those gigabit speeds in bulk transfers, but I would be skeptical when it comes to saturating the connection with a lot of smaller packet transfers.

Those radios are a big deal, as comparable SBCs for the price skip an on-board wireless stack. You get 2.4GHz Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.4 with both LE and Classic BR/EDR, and an 802.15.4 radio for Thread and Zigbee, alongside the gigabit MAC. Matter works over Wi-Fi and Thread, and going back to Bluetooth Classic for a moment, the fact it's there on an ESP32 is arguably pretty unusual. But it means older audio gear will work perfectly.

Power consumption is pretty great even with those radios, too, as Wi-Fi receive consumes between 110 mA to 117 mA depending on the mode, transmit peaks at 265 mA on 802.11b at 15 dBm, and both cores in modem-sleep at 320 MHz draw 91 mA with peripheral clocks off or 147 mA with them on. It's the power profile of a microcontroller despite having an SBC's set of peripherals.

The fact that this is called an "S31" board is a little bit strange; "S31" implies an S3 revision, despite it essentially being totally irrelevant to the regular S3. Espressif defines the S series as "high-performance feature-rich SoCs", nothing to do with instruction sets, but one big difference between both lineups were the RISC-V cores used in the C series and the Xtensa LX7 cores used in the S series.

In a comment section on Hackaday, Jeroen Domburg, Technical Marketing Manager for Espressif, said that "We actually never intended the CPU architecture to be part of the name." He also states that the core is derived from the P4's and puts the S31 at nearly twice the speed of the S3.

Unfortunately, the S31 datasheet is still out of date, stuck at version number 0.5 and a big "PRELIMINARY" watermark across the first page. it's quite detailed and mostly consistent, at least, though one example of its preliminary status is that the PSRAM is listed as having an 80 MHz maximum clock; directly at odds with Espressif's published 250 MHz PSRAM speed. To be fair, slightly messy documentation isn't particularly out of the ordinary for Espressif, but it's proof of just how early we are into the ESP32-S31's lifecycle. The Linux side is essentially just a toy to play around with, and it will be for quite a while.

The S31 isn't an SBC, but it is the first ESP32 where many of its features, from the peripherals, bandwidth, and CPU privilege model all happen to be adjacent to a modern SBC. The gap between a microcontroller with good I/O and an SBC has been closing over the past couple of years, and while you still can't run a desktop on 16 MB of PSRAM, you can get a Linux terminal up and running on it without too much trouble. And that's the first step.
aiStories.fullTranslation:
乐鑫科技（Espressif）推出了一款全新的 ESP32 芯片——ESP32-S31。该芯片配备了千兆以太网 MAC、USB 2.0 高速主机控制器、支持双插槽的 SD 卡接口以及摄像头输入接口。对于一台 Linux 单板计算机（SBC）而言，这是一套相当标准的功能配置，但出现在微控制器上却显得相当罕见。

我花过大量时间研究微控制器，通常在微控制器上能看到几个核心、少量内存、GPIO 引脚，可能还有 Wi-Fi 功能。更高级的需求通常会选用树莓派（Raspberry Pi），然而 ESP32-S31 的配置远超典型的微控制器。乐鑫还对 CPU 进行了重大改进，使其比以往任何时候都更像一台单板计算机。

ESP32-S31 最大的亮点在于其网络能力，它搭载了 1000 Mbps 以太网 MAC，相比 ESP32-P4 上较慢的 100 Mbps 实现了巨大跨越。它采用 8P8C 连接器（通常称为 RJ45），并配备利用该芯片 RGMII 接口的 PHY。正是 RGMII 实现了千兆速率；否则它将采用标准的 RMII。

除此之外还有 USB，但这并非“标准”USB。S31 配备了一个 USB 2.0 高速 OTG 控制器，并采用全尺寸 Type-A 插孔，在主机 OTG 模式下可供电 500 mA。与其并列的还有支持双槽位的 SDIO 主机控制器、支持 8 至 16 位的 DVP 摄像头接口，以及支持最高 24 位 RGB 与 I8080、MOTO6800 面板的并行 LCD 控制器。此外还有两个支持硬件蓝牙音频同步的 I2S 控制器、14 个电容式触摸通道、一个 CAN FD 控制器和四个 MCPWM 单元。

单从这份清单来看，很显然这是一款前所未见的全新类型 ESP32。有线网络？USB 主机？摄像头、显示器、音频？这里的一切都更像单板计算机而非微控制器，但这还不是全部。

在 CPU 方面，它拥有两个运行频率最高达 320 MHz 的 32 位 RISC-V 核心，每个核心均配有浮点运算单元（FPU），其中一个还带有 128 位 SIMD 数据路径，此外还有一个独立的 40 MHz 低功耗核心。每个核心配备 32KB 的 L1 指令缓存，并共享 64KB 的数据缓存。内存配置更加引人注目：S31 通过 250 MHz 8 位 DDR 接口支持高达 64 MB 的 PSRAM，同时支持最高 256MB 的闪存。在 ESP32-S3 上，PSRAM 接口是与闪存共享的，这使得此次改动成为一次相当大的提升。

乐鑫长期以来一直在使用“MMU”（内存管理单元）这一术语，包括在 ESP32-S3 和 ESP32-P4 上。然而，彼时的 MMU 只是一个将外部闪存和 PSRAM 映射到地址空间的模块，远不及现代 MMU 的复杂程度——现代 MMU 还能执行进程隔离和页表管理等任务。因此，当乐鑫宣称 S31 支持 MMU 时，表面上看起来似乎并无二致。

然而，这一次却有着重大区别。在 S31 的数据手册中，乐鑫指出这些核心支持“Sv32 两级页表地址转换”，并实现了“机器（Machine）、监管者（Supervisor）和用户（User）特权模式”。Sv32 是标准的 RISC-V 分页机制，拥有全部三种特权模式正是让常规内核能够在监管者模式下运行、同时底层固件在机器模式下运行的关键。而这正是基于 RISC-V 的 Linux 设备的工作原理。

与以往在旧款 ESP32 微控制器上运行 Linux 的各种极客式拼凑尝试不同，S31 具备更多开箱即用的原生支持。首先，乐鑫早在 8 月份就发布了基于 Buildroot 和 U-Boot 构建的 Linux BSP，其中包含内核、设备树和根文件系统。尽管乐鑫表示该方案“尚不推荐用于生产环境”，但关键在于它确实能够运行。

这也没有阻碍社区的快速迭代。其中一个移植版本已让 Linux 6.18 在监管者模式下运行，并几乎为所有硬件配备了可用驱动。另一个基于 Linux 7.1 的版本则支持连接 800x480 分辨率的 LCD 屏幕并显示控制台终端。能够外接显示屏、使用有线以太网、外接鼠标和键盘，听起来完全更像是一台单板计算机，而非微控制器。

不过，在内存方面，S31 开始显露出局限性：芯片内置 512KB SRAM，提供集成 16MB 或 32MB 封装内 PSRAM 的两个版本。它所能支持的最大内存为 64MB，且完全没有 DRAM 控制器。与拥有 512MB 内存的 Milk-V Duo S 等竞品相比，竞争对手会很快提醒你：ESP32-S31 归根结底仍然是一款微控制器。

这正是为什么那些 Linux 构建版本会从闪存中直接执行内核，以避免消耗宝贵的 PSRAM。此外，板上没有配备 GPU 或 NPU；虽然 ESP32-P4 配备了视频编码与 MIPI 接口，但在 S31 上，这些被替换成了额外的无线射频模块。尽管它仍配备 JPEG 编解码器、2D 像素处理加速器和 2D DMA，但这并不足以支撑起完整的 Linux 桌面环境。

其时钟频率也让千兆以太网网卡的能力引发了一些疑问。在 320 MHz 下，每个最大尺寸以太网帧大约分配到 3900 个 CPU 周期，而最小尺寸帧大约只有 215 个周期。凭借 PSRAM 500 MB/s 的理论最大吞吐量，在大文件批量传输时或可接近千兆速率，但面对大量小数据包传输时，能否跑满千兆带宽令人怀疑。

那些无线射频模块是一大杀手锏，因为同等价位的单板计算机往往省去了板载无线协议栈。除了千兆 MAC，你还能获得 2.4GHz Wi-Fi 6、同时支持 LE 与经典 BR/EDR 的蓝牙 5.4，以及用于 Thread 和 Zigbee 的 802.15.4 射频模块。Matter 协议可在 Wi-Fi 和 Thread 上运行；再谈谈经典蓝牙，它出现在 ESP32 上可以说相当罕见，但这意味着它可以完美兼容老旧的音频设备。

即使搭载了这些射频模块，其功耗表现依然十分出色：Wi-Fi 接收功耗根据工作模式介于 110 mA 至 117 mA 之间；在 802.11b（15 dBm）下发送峰值功耗为 265 mA；双核在 320 MHz 调制解调器睡眠（modem-sleep）状态下，外设时钟关闭时电流为 91 mA，开启时为 147 mA。尽管具备单板计算机级别的外设配置，它依然保持着微控制器级别的功耗特性。

这款芯片被命名为“S31”略显奇特；“S31”听起来像 S3 的修订版，但它在本质上与普通的 S3 毫无关联。乐鑫将 S 系列定义为“高性能且功能丰富的 SoC”，与指令集无关，但此前两个产品线的一大差异在于：C 系列采用 RISC-V 核心，而 S 系列则采用 Xtensa LX7 核心。

在 Hackaday 的评论区中，乐鑫技术营销经理 Jeroen Domburg 表示：“我们实际上从未打算将 CPU 架构作为命名的一部分。”他还指出，该核心源自 P4 的架构，使 S31 的运行速度接近 S3 的两倍。

遗憾的是，S31 的数据手册依然过时，停留在 0.5 版本，且首页带有醒目的“初步”（PRELIMINARY）水印。至少它相当详尽且基本保持一致，不过体现其初步状态的一个例子是：手册中列出的 PSRAM 最大时钟频率为 80 MHz，这与乐鑫（Espressif）公布的 250 MHz PSRAM 速度直接冲突。平心而论，文档略显混乱对乐鑫来说并不算特别反常，但这也足以证明我们目前处于 ESP32-S31 生命周期的极早期阶段。Linux 端基本上只是一个用于探索体验的玩具，而且在相当长一段时间内都会如此。

S31 并不是单板计算机（SBC），但它是第一款从外设、带宽到 CPU 特权模型等诸多特性都恰好与现代 SBC 极其接近的 ESP32。在过去几年中，拥有良好 I/O 能力的微控制器与 SBC 之间的差距一直在缩小；尽管你仍然无法在 16 MB 的 PSRAM 上运行桌面系统，但毫无压力地启动并运行一个 Linux 终端已经完全可以做到。而这正是迈出的第一步。

aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

The new frontier AI model should arrive long before the end of 2026.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Jess Weatherbed

Google is reportedly nearing the launch of its long awaited Gemini 4 model, after dawdling behind rival developers on flagship AI releases. Speaking with The Information during his first media appearance as the leader of Google’s DeepMind division, Koray Kavukcuoglu said that Gemini 4 is currently in its refinement stage, and that the company is aiming to launch the model “much earlier” than the end of the year.

“Our intention is to, like — as soon as possible — to release an early post-training output because we see the results and we are excited,” Kavukcuoglu told the publication, adding that Google would “continue the fast-paced iterations” going forward. This hopefully marks Google returning to a more consistent AI release timeline following a shakeup at DeepMind’s top leadership, with former AI head Demis Hassabis stepping down in August after announcing that “great progress” was being made on Gemini 4.

Google hasn’t released a new flagship AI model since the Gemini 3 series in November 2025. OpenAI’s GPT-6 and Anthropic’s Mythos series models have launched since then. Both outperform Gemini 3 and give the rival AI providers a sizable lead against Google in the AI race. Google CEO Sundar Pichai said at the I/O event in May that a major Gemini 3.5 Pro update would be coming in June to help bridge the gap, but the model was never rolled out.

Kavukcuoglu said the company “took a little bit of a step back” to focus on introducing faster, less powerful Flash models instead of releasing Gemini 3.5 Pro. When asked whether he was concerned about Google falling behind its rivals on AI development, he told The Information that “In my mind, it’s a certainty that we are always gonna be at the frontier.”

据报道，在旗舰AI版本发布方面落后于竞争对手之后，谷歌正接近推出其备受期待的 Gemini 4 模型。科拉伊·卡武克库奥卢（Koray Kavukcuoglu）在出任谷歌 DeepMind 部门负责人后的首次媒体亮相中接受《The Information》采访时表示，Gemini 4 目前正处于优化调整阶段，公司的目标是在年底前“早得多”的时候推出该模型。

“我们的意图是，尽快——比如尽快——发布早期后训练成果，因为我们看到了效果并且感到非常兴奋，”卡武克库奥卢向该媒体表示，并补充称谷歌未来将“继续进行快节奏的迭代”。在 DeepMind 高层领导层发生变动之后，这有望标志着谷歌重回更具连贯性的 AI 发布时间表；前 AI 负责人德米斯·哈萨比斯（Demis Hassabis）在宣布 Gemini 4 正在取得“巨大进展”后，于8月辞职。

自2025年11月推出 Gemini 3 系列以来，谷歌尚未发布过新的旗舰 AI 模型。此后，OpenAI 的 GPT-6 和 Anthropic 的 Mythos 系列模型相继推出。这两者性能均超越了 Gemini 3，并在 AI 竞赛中为这些竞争对手赢得了对抗谷歌的显著领先优势。谷歌首席执行官桑达尔·皮查伊（Sundar Pichai）曾在5月的 I/O 大会上表示，Gemini 3.5 Pro 的重大更新将于6月推出以帮助缩小差距，但该模型最终从未面世。

卡武克库奥卢表示，公司当时“稍稍退后了一步”，将重点转向推出速度更快、算力要求较低的 Flash 模型，而不是发布 Gemini 3.5 Pro。当被问及是否担心谷歌在 AI 研发上落后于竞争对手时，他向《The Information》表示：“在我看来，我们始终处于最前沿是毋庸置疑的。”
